title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch turns cell leakage into retention
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #13 Other way round: hang each storage node between two back-to-back nanoscale Esaki (band-to-band tunnel) diodes so their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages. Leakage then pulls the node toward its stored value instead of away from it; the diodes are doped for ~1 pA valley current, and read/write still go through the normal access transistor. Contradiction resolved: tiny capacitor vs. no refresh.
why: Fact 3: eliminates refresh (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) for ~1 mW/Gb holding power; Cs can shrink 3-5x because no decay margin is needed (fact 1).

title: Matryoshka coaxial multi-shell capacitor by sequential annular ALD casting
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: inside each pillar footprint grow three concentric electrode shells separated by dielectric, alternately strapped to storage node and plate (interdigitated coax), by repeating ALD electrode/dielectric/sacrificial-carbon fill and recess-etch cycles. Contradiction resolved: more electrode area vs. same footprint and lower aspect ratio.
why: Fact 1: ~2.5-3x Cs per footprint, or equal Cs at AR ~30:1 instead of 60-75:1, easing etch, bending and collapse.

title: Antiferroelectric double-loop capacitor that buffers leakage with phase-transition charge
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric dielectric with the plate biased so writing a '1' crosses the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition and stores extra polarization charge (~10-20 uC/cm2). As the node leaks down to the backward-switching field, the polarization collapses and releases charge, clamping the node voltage like a reservoir; no remanence means no imprint or nonvolatility side-effects.
why: Fact 1: effective charge per area ~3-5x linear ZrO2 at the same voltage, and the built-in charge reservoir stretches retention 2-4x (fact 3).

title: Ferroelectric/paraelectric superlattice in stabilized negative capacitance, effective k ~80
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: stack ~1-nm HZO ferroelectric layers between Al2O3/ZrO2 paraelectric layers sized so the ferroelectric sits on its stabilized negative-capacitance branch, making the series stack capacitance larger than either layer alone, with no hysteresis. Contradiction resolved: thick (low-leakage) dielectric vs. high capacitance.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: reaching k_eff 60-90 at ~6 nm physical thickness cuts tunneling-leakage tail ~10x versus equal-EOT ZrO2.

title: Image-sensor pinned well with source-follower readout replaces the capacitor
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality + #2 Taking out: borrow the CMOS image sensor 4T pixel and store the bit as ~500-2,000 electrons in a buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer (dark current ~aA, since the surface traps are pinned), transfer it to a floating diffusion through a transfer gate and read it through an in-cell source follower. Gain readout, not charge sharing, senses it, so no tall capacitor is needed; the shrink target is a vertical pinned pillar of ~40 nm.
why: Facts 1 and 3: removes the 60-75:1 capacitor and drops leakage ~1,000x (refresh every seconds), at the cost of 3-4 transistors per cell; today's 0.5-um pixels are far too large, which is the main risk.

title: Bistable buckled 2D-membrane nanodrum stores the bit as curvature
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution + #14 Spheroidality: a pre-compressed few-layer hBN or graphene membrane over a ~30-nm cavity buckles either up or down; an electrostatic pulse from the top or bottom electrode snaps it over, and its capacitance to the bottom electrode reads the state without disturbing it. No charge is stored, so nothing leaks.
why: Facts 3 and 8: zero refresh and non-destructive read; 2D membranes survive >10^12 flex cycles; back-end array over periphery at ~4F2.

title: Ionic-liquid nanopore double-layer cell stores charge at angstrom separation
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics (liquid replaces solid): fill a sealed ~20-nm blocking-electrode pore per cell with a high-conductivity ionic liquid whose electric double layer (~0.5-nm Helmholtz gap) gives 10-20 uF/cm2 at under 1 V, versus ~8 uF/cm2 for best solid high-k. Contradiction resolved: more charge vs. lower voltage.
why: Facts 1 and 10: ~2x charge per area at sub-1 V; charging RC estimated 30-300 ns in a pore, so speed and self-discharge are the open risks.

title: Colloidal-sphere inverse-opal electrode gives area without a high-aspect etch
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality + #31 Porous materials: self-assemble 5-8-nm silica nanospheres in each shallow cell well, ALD-coat TiN/ZrO2/TiN through the interstices, then dissolve the spheres to leave a 3D inverse-opal capacitor whose curved shells multiply area ~6-10x per volume at AR <10:1.
why: Facts 1 and 4: replaces the 60-75:1 pillar etch and its tool capital with a self-assembled scaffold, giving the same Cs in a squat cell.

title: Nanomechanical parametron stores the bit as oscillation phase
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #15 Dynamics: revive Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale. Each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at 2f by a shared wordline AC drive, ringing at f in one of two phases (0 or 180 degrees); phase is the bit, the pump continuously regenerates it, and a small injected signal picks the phase on write.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no transistor leakage tail and no refresh, plus native majority-logic in memory; pump power and density are the risks.

title: Circulating CCD loop memory with refresh built into the motion
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: store bits as charge packets marching around short (64-256 stage) buried-channel CCD loops at ~2F gate pitch with no per-bit transistor; one floating-gate amplifier per loop regenerates each packet as it passes, so refresh is inherent and there is no capacitor or access device.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 7: ~2-3F2 per bit with no capacitor; GHz loop rotation gives tens of ns average latency, best for streaming AI weights.

title: Vacuum-sealed storage node with field-emission nanogap access switch
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): suspend each storage node on thin oxide posts inside a sealed nano-vacuum cavity so no junction or dielectric film touches it, and access it through a gated vacuum-channel field-emission diode with a <50-nm gap that conducts only above its turn-on field. Vacuum has no traps or band tails, so hold leakage is set by Fowler-Nordheim at low field (aA-class).
why: Fact 3: refresh intervals of minutes to hours; the vacuum switch's extremely steep turn-on also helps fact 10.

title: Crested van der Waals tunnel barrier: thick at hold, thin at write
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: write the storage node through an hBN/MoSe2/hBN 'crested' tunnel stack whose barrier peak collapses under write field (current up ~10^8x per volt) but stays thick at hold bias. Dangling-bond-free vdW interfaces generate far fewer traps than oxide flash, targeting >10^15 cycles.
why: Fact 3: a two-terminal selector with negligible hold leakage replaces the leaky access transistor, enabling 4F2 crosspoint charge cells.

title: VO2 hysteresis latch held bistable by the chip's own waste heat
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #36 Phase transition: dope VO2 (W/Ge) so its 5-10 K insulator-metal hysteresis loop sits at the stack's operating temperature, so each nano-VO2 cell stays insulating or metallic indefinitely while warm. Write '1' with a ns Joule pulse, reset with a piezo-strain gate pulse that shifts the loop, and read resistance non-destructively.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no refresh, non-destructive read; idle cost is heat the accelerator already makes; data are volatile at power-off like DRAM.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall bit in ScAlN or lithium niobate nanomesa
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: in each single-crystal nanomesa, a ns voltage pulse creates or erases a charged domain wall that conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; the bit is wall present/absent, read non-destructively by a small current. Switching is ferroelectric with no ion motion, and CMOS-friendly wurtzite ScAlN is the target host.
why: Fact 8: non-destructive read with no restore; fact 3: nonvolatile, no refresh; crosspoint 4F2 with one lithography level.

title: Non-collinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn bit with zero stray field
idea: TRIZ #13 Other way round: instead of a ferromagnet (MRAM, already examined), store the bit in the octupole order of a non-collinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn) switched by spin-orbit torque from an underlying heavy-metal or topological line and read by its large anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance. Zero net moment means no stray-field coupling and ~10-ps switching.
why: Facts 3 and 9: nonvolatile with no refresh, immune to row-hammer-style neighbor coupling, and packable at 2-3F2 because there are no stray fields.

title: Few-electron quantum-dot bit sensed by an adjacent single-electron transistor
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation taken to the limit: store each bit as ~5-10 electrons on a <3-nm Si or SnO2 quantum dot whose Coulomb charging energy (>100 meV) blocks leakage, and sense it non-destructively with an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current swings ~10x per electron.
why: Facts 1 and 10: ~1,000x less charge than a 5-fF cell, so CV2 write energy drops ~100x and no capacitor is needed; room-temperature dot uniformity is the risk.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer adds quantized charge states to every capacitor
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: graft a self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene dyads) onto the storage electrode so each molecule adds 1-2 electrons at fixed oxidation potentials. Charge density reaches ~10-30 uC/cm2 versus ~5 for high-k at 1 V, and the discrete potentials give native 2-bit cells.
why: Fact 1: 3-5x Cs per area; fact 10: multi-level storage at fixed, low voltages.

title: Bootstrapped T-switch gain cell zeroes leakage across its write path
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality + #25 Self-service: write the gain-cell storage node through two series transistors and drive their middle node from the cell's own source-follower output, the guard trick from electrometers and sample-and-hold circuits. The inner transistor then sees ~0 V drain-source, so subthreshold leakage collapses.
why: Fact 3: leakage down ~50-100x, stretching refresh from 64 ms to seconds with plain Si or oxide transistors.

title: Percolation-edge metal-nanoisland dielectric with giant effective permittivity
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: disperse 1-2-nm Ru or TiN nanoislands in ZrO2 just below the percolation threshold, using ALD nucleation-delay cycles, so percolative/Maxwell-Wagner effects push effective k toward 150-1,000 while isolated islands leave no continuous leakage path.
why: Fact 1: even k~150 would let pillar AR drop to ~25:1; hopping leakage and ns-scale frequency dispersion are the risks.

title: Eight-segment self-clearing capacitor survives dielectric defects at thinner EOT
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation + #25 Self-service: split each cell's capacitor into 8 parallel sub-capacitors, each tied in by a ~2-nm top-electrode neck that vaporizes like a metallized-film capacitor's self-clearing spot when a defect shorts it, so the cell keeps 7/8 of its charge instead of dying.
why: Fact 1 and yield: EOT can shrink 20-30% (Cs +25-40%) because tail defects no longer kill cells; fewer redundant rows needed.

title: Ephemeral 1 fF cells for millisecond-lifetime AI activations
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: build sub-arrays whose cells hold only ~1 fF and keep data ~1-5 ms with no refresh at all, reserved for activations and KV tiles that are written once and consumed within a millisecond. The compiler tags data lifetimes, and the controller rejects stale reads by timestamp.
why: Facts 1 and 3: capacitor 4-5x smaller (AR ~15:1), zero refresh energy, ~2x density for transient data.

title: Self-rolled-up nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitor in every cell
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #7 Nesting: deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/SiN multilayer flat with no deep etch, then release a sacrificial layer so built-in strain rolls it into a 5-10-turn tube; each turn adds electrode area, and lateral rolls suit horizontal 3D DRAM tiers.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 4: ~10x area per footprint from planar deposition and release, replacing 70:1 etching; scaling roll diameter to tens of nm is the risk.

title: Epitaxial all-perovskite SrRuO3/SrTiO3 capacitor without the interface dead layer
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: make electrodes and dielectric from one perovskite family (SrRuO3/SrTiO3/SrRuO3) grown coherently so no low-k interfacial dead layer forms; thin SrTiO3 then keeps k ~200+ instead of collapsing to ~50 as it does between TiN electrodes.
why: Fact 1: k~200 beats the k~70 target, so pillar AR could fall to ~20:1; low-temperature epitaxy on 3D surfaces is the risk.

title: Peel-and-relaminate van der Waals storage film on a reusable CMOS base
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #34 Discarding and recovering: build the bit-storing layer (hBN/MoS2 gain-cell or capacitor film) as a vdW stack held only by van der Waals forces and edge contacts to pads on a finished CMOS periphery wafer. When cells wear out, or a better storage film appears, the stack is peeled with thermal-release tape and a fresh one laminated. Repairable by design: the storage element is the swappable consumable.
why: Facts 4 and 7: reuses capital-heavy periphery and logic silicon (~49% of die) across storage generations; the film strips with no acid, so it is recyclable.

title: Wordline-as-heater in-field anneal rejuvenates aged capacitor dielectrics
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: drive controlled current through spare wordline/plate metal to heat one air-gap-isolated sub-array to ~300-400 C for milliseconds, annealing out trap and oxygen-vacancy build-up in the capacitor dielectric and access-transistor interface after its data are moved to a neighbor mat. The aged storage element heals in place instead of being scrapped.
why: Fact 3: reverses retention-tail drift; extends module life ~2-3x so the same wafer starts serve longer.

title: Niobium-oxide cell with self-healing solid-electrolyte top plate
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: copy the solid niobium electrolytic capacitor. Anodize a Nb storage electrode to Nb2O5 (k~40) and use a MnO2 or conductive-polymer top plate; at any leakage hot spot the fault current itself converts MnO2 to insulating Mn2O3 (or de-dopes the polymer), sealing the defect, and an in-field 're-forming' pulse regrows thinned oxide by anodization.
why: Fact 1: k~40 with self-sealed defect tail lets the dielectric run ~30% thinner (Cs +30-50%); repair is built into the storage element.

title: Sixty-four independently biased plate segments isolate shorted capacitor blocks
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: break the array's common capacitor plate into 64 switch-fed segments per bank. A plate-to-node short, today a die-killer because the plate is shared, is isolated in the field by floating that segment and remapping its 1/64 of the bank to spare rows, so the die is repaired rather than scrapped.
why: Yield and repairability: recovers dies lost to plate shorts (est. several % yield) and keeps aging parts in service.

title: Mono-family silicon storage element recyclable straight to solar-grade silicon
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: build the storage element only from Si, SiO2, Si3N4 and doped poly-Si (ONO dielectric, poly electrodes, no Hf/Zr/Ru/W/TiN) and accept the low k by reading with a gain cell instead of charge sharing. Shredded end-of-life dies go straight to silicon refining after an HF strip, with no heavy-metal contamination.
why: Scarce resources and recyclability: removes tungsten (China ~80%), Ru and Hf; gain readout tolerates ~0.5 fF storage.

title: Ruthenium electrodes reclaimed as volatile RuO4 into ALD precursor
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: specify Ru electrodes (which template rutile TiO2 with k~80-100) and design the recycling route in from day one. Ozone-treat shredded dies at ~100 C so Ru leaves as volatile RuO4, trap it in a cold scrubber and convert it directly back to Ru ALD precursor, closing the loop for a metal mined at only ~30 t/yr.
why: Fact 1 via high-k rutile, without the supply risk of a South-Africa-concentrated metal; near-total Ru recovery.

title: UV-transparent lid lets depots erase trapped charge in oxide storage layers
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (optical for electrical): for back-end oxide-semiconductor storage tiers that sit at the top of the stack, package them under a fused-silica window like an EPROM; in a repair depot, deep-UV de-traps charge accumulated in the gate dielectric and channel, restoring threshold voltage and retention without electrical stress.
why: Fact 3 drift reversal and module reuse; turns threshold-voltage drift from a scrap cause into a serviceable condition.

title: Scheduled reverse-polarity detox pulses push oxygen vacancies back
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #9 Prior anti-action: during idle windows the controller swaps plate bias so every capacitor in a mat sees a brief inverted field (~-1.2 V, ~1 us), driving field-drifted oxygen vacancies and trapped charge back toward their as-built distribution before they form leakage percolation paths.
why: Fact 3: reverses the dominant wear mode instead of over-provisioning margin; could allow ~20% thinner dielectric and higher Cs.

title: Water-dissolvable transient storage cells for short-service bulk buffer memory
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: fabricate cells from the 'transient electronics' palette (Si nanomembrane transistors, MgO dielectric, Mo/Mg electrodes on a polymer handle) for 2-3-year bulk buffer memory; at end of life the boards dissolve in buffered water, leaving Si and Mo for recovery.
why: Capital and recyclability: low-temperature, low-cost process for bulk capacity; full material recovery; encapsulation life is the risk.

title: Re-meltable tin-bismuth plate fill replaces tungsten and drains out
idea: TRIZ #29 Hydraulics + #36 Phase transition: pressure-infiltrate molten Sn-Bi eutectic (139 C) over a wetting liner to fill capacitor interiors and the common plate instead of CVD W/TiN. It is solid in service, can be reflowed to heal voids, and is melted out at end of life for direct reuse.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and recyclability; avoids WF6 fluorine damage; ~100 MPa Laplace pressure for 10-nm pores is the risk.

title: Pre-implanted cleave plane lets storage substrates be reclaimed repeatedly
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: build the storage array in a thin single-crystal layer transferred by hydrogen-implant ion cut onto a handle wafer that carries a second pre-implanted weak plane; at end of life or after test failure, the handle is split there, re-polished and reused 5-10 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts Spruce Pine quartz-crucible and polysilicon demand per GB ~5x through handle reuse.

title: Bimorph stress layer self-delaminates the storage tier during recycling bake
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: insert a high-CTE metal / low-CTE nitride bimorph between the storage-capacitor tier and the CMOS logic. It is inert below the 450 C back-end budget, but a 550 C recycling bake drives mismatch strain past interface toughness so the capacitor tier (Zr, Ru, Ti) curls off as flakes.
why: Recyclability: two clean streams (silicon logic, metal-oxide storage) for cheap high-purity recovery of scarce metals.

title: Ceria oxygen buffer refillable like a catalytic converter's storage
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior anti-action: insert a ~0.5-nm CeO2 interlayer into the ZrO2 stack. As with the oxygen-storage capacity in car catalytic converters, Ce4+/Ce3+ swaps donate oxygen to fill vacancies formed under field stress, and a periodic thermal anneal pulls oxygen back from an RuO2/TiON electrode reservoir to recharge the buffer.
why: Facts 1 and 3: slows leakage-tail growth so thinner, higher-Cs dielectrics survive 10 years; a rechargeable buffer is repair by design.

title: Dormant spare storage tiers swap in when a 3D tier wears out
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: in stacked-tier 3D DRAM, fabricate 2 unpowered spare tiers per ~32; on-die retention monitors detect a tier whose leakage tail has drifted, and a nonvolatile tier map swaps a spare in while data copy in the background.
why: Fact 2: makes 3D tiers field-repairable where laser fuses can't reach; ~6% area buys ~2-3x service life.

title: Overvoltage burn turns flickering VRT cells into deterministic hard faults
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: variable-retention-time cells flicker between leaky and good and escape test. During in-field maintenance, hit any cell flagged even once with a controlled ~2.5-3 V stress pulse that breaks its weak dielectric down to a hard short, so the next scrub always detects it and maps it to a spare.
why: Fact 3: refresh interval can follow the normal population, not the VRT tail, roughly halving refresh energy; repair becomes deterministic.

title: Nested charge-trap shadow layer preserves data through heal cycles
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed a ~2-nm SiN charge-trap layer inside each capacitor dielectric so that before a repair anneal, detox or module removal the controller programs a nonvolatile shadow copy of every bit with a Fowler-Nordheim burst, then restores it afterwards. Repairs no longer need external data migration, and the shadow is used rarely so its endurance suffices.
why: Repairability: makes in-place healing practical on full arrays; also gives power-loss persistence for free.

title: Deliberately weakened canary capacitors trigger targeted per-mat rejuvenation
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: place a few 'canary' copies of the storage element in every mat, built with ~20% thinner dielectric or smaller Cs so they age first; their retention, checked during refresh, triggers the heal action (anneal, detox pulse or spare swap) for that mat only.
why: Repairability: predictive maintenance instead of worst-case guard bands costing ~10-15% density or refresh energy.

title: Age-adaptive cells step down from multi-level to binary storage
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: store 2 bits per capacitor (4 charge levels sensed against a ramped reference) while the array is young; as retention tails widen, the controller re-formats aging pages to 1 bit/cell with large margin, and later to a refresh-heavy cold tier, rather than failing the module.
why: Density ~2x early in life and ~2-3x longer service life through graceful downgrade.

title: Retired DRAM reborn as unclonable-identity and true-random chips
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: the retention-decay map of worn storage cells is random, unique and hard to clone. Recertify end-of-life DRAM dies as PUF identity chips and decay-based true-random generators for IoT security, priced above scrap value.
why: Recyclability and economics: a second life for dies otherwise shredded; raises the residual value of every wafer start.

title: Memory leasing with depot rejuvenation and retention re-binning
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: makers lease socketed DDR/CXL modules to hyperscalers and take them back every ~3 years; depots map retention, bulk-anneal to heal dielectric traps, re-bin by retention class and re-lease to less demanding tiers.
why: Usable supply: ~1.5-2x more service-years per wafer start during the 4x price spike; better capital efficiency.

title: JEDEC heal command and storage-cell health telemetry standard
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: standardize a host-visible cell-health report (per-mat retention-tail percentiles) plus a REJUV command class (thermal, detox pulse, spare swap), so the OS can schedule storage-element repair the way SSDs schedule TRIM and garbage collection; CHIPS-funded buyers require it in procurement.
why: Repairability at fleet scale: turns per-device heal mechanisms into a usable ecosystem, extending module life.

title: Fluorescent tracers encode storage-stack chemistry for automated recycling sorting
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: dope each die's passivation with distinct carbon-dot or Mn:ZnS emission signatures that encode its storage-stack chemistry (Ru vs TiN electrodes, Hf vs Zr dielectric); shredder lines sort fragments optically into chemistry-matched streams for metal recovery.
why: Recyclability and scarce resources: higher-purity recovered Ru/Hf/Zr at low sorting cost.

title: Contactless coupled storage dies lift off for replacement
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension + #28 Mechanics substitution: stack storage dies with no TSVs or hybrid bonds; signals cross by inductive/capacitive coupling (~0.1 pJ/bit), power arrives through a few spring micro-contacts, and a reversible clamp holds the stack, so a worn storage die is lifted out and replaced while the logic base die stays.
why: Fact 6: avoids the HBM TSV tax (~3x area per bit, 20-30% yield loss) and allows known-good-die replacement instead of scrapping whole stacks.
